title: Revisiting DETR Pre-training for Object Detection

problem.summary: The paper argues that self-supervised Transformer pre-training for DETR detectors, exemplified by DETReg, fails to improve strong DETR models such as H-Deformable-DETR under full-data conditions, because its Selective Search box proposals give noisy localization targets and feature reconstruction gives a weak classification target.
statements: DETReg pre-training does not improve, and can even hurt, the performance of strong DETR variants like H-Deformable-DETR on COCO.
Unsupervised region proposals from Selective Search are unreliable boxes that produce noisy localization pre-training targets.
Feature reconstruction supplies weak semantic information that is not an efficient classification target for pre-training.

evidence.quote: Regrettably, DETReg proves inadequate in enhancing the performance of robust DETR-based models under full data conditions.
We pinpoint the crux of the issue as originating from unreliable box proposals generated by unsupervised methods like Selective Search, which contribute to noisy localization targets

the weak semantic information provided through feature reconstruction which is not an efficient classification target either. These drawbacks make the self-supervised pretraining methods ineffective when applied to an already strong DETR model.

background.summary: The work builds on DETR, Deformable-DETR and H-Deformable-DETR, and on DETR pre-training methods UP-DETR, DETReg and Siamese DETR, claiming these pretext tasks only help weak DETR variants and that self-training with pseudo-labels is an underexplored alternative for pre-training the Transformer part.

relatedWork.name: Deformable-DETR
relatedWork.relation: prior DETR variant with multi-scale deformable attention
relatedWork.quote: Deformable-DETR (Zhu et al., 2020) proposes a novel multi-scale deformable self/cross-attention to focus on a sparse set of important sampling points around a reference point.

relatedWork.name: DETReg
relatedWork.relation: representative self-supervised pre-training baseline being revisited
relatedWork.quote: DETReg (Bar et al., 2022) refines the pretext task by using unsupervised region proposals from Selective Search (Uijlings et al., 2013) instead of random patches

relatedWork.name: H-Deformable-DETR
relatedWork.relation: strongest downstream detector used as the test bed
relatedWork.quote: and Group-DETR (Chen et al., 2022) propose to train with more queries in the transformer decoder with an additional one-to-many matching scheme

relatedWork.name: NoisyStudent
relatedWork.relation: prior self-training scheme contrasted with the proposed simple variant
relatedWork.quote: A common self-training method is NoisyStudent (Xie et al., 2020), which trains a teacher model on labeled data and uses it to generate pseudolabels on unlabeled images.

evidence.quote: Several recent works have improved DETR-based object detection models by performing self-supervised pretraining on the Transformer encoder and decoder while freezing the backbone.
However, these pre-training methods only yield minor improvements to a strong DETR variant like DeformableDETR.

Unlike these complex self-training schemes that use an iterative approach to refine pseudo-labels, we propose a Simple Self-training scheme that generates pseudo-labels only once by keeping a fixed number of the most confident predictions.

solution.summary: The paper proposes Simple Self-training: an off-the-shelf COCO-trained H-Deformable-DETR predicts top pseudo-boxes with pseudo-class labels on a pre-training dataset (default Objects365), and these replace DETReg's Selective Search boxes and object-embedding targets when pre-training the DETR encoder and decoder.
solution.approach: Replace noisy unsupervised pre-training targets with one-off pseudo-box and pseudo-class predictions from a frozen COCO detector, optionally extended with synthetic image-to-text/text-to-image pre-training data.
components: pseudo-box localization targets from a COCO detector
pseudo-class classification targets replacing object-embedding reconstruction
synthetic pre-training datasets from LLaVA captions with ControlNet/SDXL

evidence.quote: To fix this, we propose to use a COCO object detector to get more accurate pseudo-boxes with informative pseudo-class labels.
Our findings reveal that a Simple Self-training scheme, employing pseudo-box and pseudo-class predictions as pre-training targets, outperforms the DETReg approach in various settings.
The unsupervised box proposals like Selective Search boxes are of very low quality.
our Simple Self-training method directly generate the pseudo-labels for one time without those tricks, resulting in a much simpler approach.

experiments.summary: The authors pre-train DETR, Deformable-DETR and H-Deformable-DETR on ImageNet or Objects365, fine-tune on COCO and PASCAL VOC, and compare against DETReg and supervised upper bounds, plus ablations on dataset choice, pseudo-box count, encoder vs decoder pre-training, low-data regimes and synthetic data.

evidence.quote: The culmination of these endeavors results in a remarkable AP score of 59.3% on the COCO val set, outperforming HDeformable-DETR + Swin-L without pre-training by 1.4%.
Our Simple Self-training approach significantly boosts the performance of H-Deformable-DETR from 57.9% to 59.3% with fewer training epochs.
the DETReg pre-training fails to bring improvement to the from scratch baseline on the COCO benchmark, while can get small gains on the PASCAL VOC benchmark.

limitations.summary: Simple Self-training still sits just below the fully supervised pre-training upper bound, its gains depend on the quality of pseudo-boxes from COCO detectors, and synthetic data built from Objects365 captions works worse than COCO-based synthetic data.
items: Supervised use of ground-truth targets remains slightly better than Simple Self-training (upper bound).
Pseudo-boxes beyond the top 30 likely carry low confidence and inject noise into the targets.
Pre-training with Objects365-derived synthetic images underperforms COCO-derived synthetic images.
Reported gains use a small pre-training schedule (3 epochs) and default batch size 16.

evidence.quote: achieve an upper-bound performance that is only slightly better than our Simple Self-training strategy.
the predictions beyond the top 30 may have low confidence and less meaningful information, as a result of incorporating noise into the pseudo-box target.
They are not as good as pretraining with COCO-based synthetic data on both downstream benchmarks.
We expect our approach to achieve better results with bigger batch size and epoch number

futureDirections.direction: Extend DETR pre-training beyond detection to a broader set of vision tasks such as instance segmentation and pose estimation.
futureDirections.quote: Moving forward, we plan to extend DETR pre-training to encompass a broader spectrum of vision tasks, such as instance segmentation and pose estimation.

futureDirections.direction: Prompt the community to re-evaluate how well existing self-supervised pre-training methods really work with strong DETR models.
futureDirections.quote: We hope our work can stimulate the research community to reassess the actual capacity of existing selfsupervised pre-training methods when employed in the context of strong DETR models

equations.expr: argmin_{theta_E, theta_D, Q} sum_i L_pre(z_i, y_i)

equations.name: Hungarian label assignment
equations.expr: sigma_i = argmin_{sigma in Sigma_k} sum_j L_match(y_ij, z_i,sigma(j))

equations.name: Simple Self-training loss
equations.expr: sum_j lambda_c L_cls(c_pseudo, c_pred) + lambda_b * 1{c_pseudo != empty} L_box(b_pseudo, b_pred)
